requestKey: Daily stretches for people who sit all day|sway.day|sample2

payload.text:
Great plan. Here’s a simple, joint-friendly routine designed for desk-sitters. No equipment needed beyond a chair and a doorway. Use what you like and build the habit.

How to use this
- Frequency: Do the 2-minute Microbreak every 30–60 minutes. Do the 10–15 minute Routine once per day.
- Intensity: Mild-to-moderate stretch, no pain or pins-and-needles. Breathe slowly; exhale tension.
- Holds/reps: Static stretches 20–45 seconds, 1–2 rounds per side. Mobility moves 6–10 slow reps.

2-minute Desk Microbreak (anytime)
1) Posture reset + breaths (20–30 seconds)
   - Sit tall at the edge of your chair, feet flat. Inhale through the nose, long exhale, imagine “growing tall.”
2) Chin tucks (10 reps)
   - Gently draw head straight back (give yourself a “double chin”), hold 2–3 seconds, release.
3) Neck side bend stretch (20 seconds/side)
   - Ear toward shoulder; keep shoulders relaxed. Optional: light downward reach with opposite hand.
4) Shoulder openers (30–40 seconds total)
   - 10 scapular squeezes (pinch shoulder blades, 2-second hold), then 5–8 big shoulder rolls each way.
5) Thoracic extension over chair (20 seconds)
   - Hands behind head, hinge upper back over chair back, open chest; small range.
6) Wrist/forearm stretch (15–20 seconds/side)
   - Arm straight, palm up, gently pull fingers back; then palm down.

Daily mobility routine (10–15 minutes)
Upper body and spine
1) Cat–Cow (8–10 reps)
   - On hands/knees or seated: alternate rounding and gently extending your spine.
2) Thread-the-Needle (30–45 seconds/side)
   - From all-fours, slide right arm under left, rest shoulder/head, breathe into upper back.
3) Doorway pec stretch (30–45 seconds/side)
   - Forearm on doorframe, elbow ~90°, step through to open chest; keep ribs down.

Hips and legs
4) Hip flexor lunge stretch (30–45 seconds/side)
   - Half-kneeling or split-stance. Tuck pelvis (think “zip up jeans”), squeeze back-side glute to feel front-hip stretch.
   - Can be done standing with back knee straight if kneeling isn’t comfy.
5) 90/90 hip switches (6–10 reps)
   - Sit with both knees bent at 90°, rotate legs side-to-side; pause where you feel tight.
6) Figure-4 glute stretch (30–45 seconds/side)
   - Sit, cross ankle over opposite knee; hinge forward keeping back long.
7) Hamstring stretch with strap or seated (30–45 seconds/side)
   - Keep a soft knee; hinge at hips rather than rounding the back.
8) Calf stretch (30 seconds/side)
   - Lean into wall with back heel down; switch. Option: bend back knee slightly to target soleus.

Ankles, wrists, and eyes
9) Ankle circles or “ABCs” (30 seconds/side)
10) Wrist flexion/extension stretch (15–20 seconds/side)
11) Eye reset (20-20-20 rule)
    - Every ~20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.

Optional add-ons (1–3 minutes)
- Thoracic extension on foam roller or two stacked towels (gentle, 3–4 slow breaths in each spot).
- Supported squat hold facing a desk for counterbalance (20–30 seconds) to open ankles/hips.
- Gentle hang from a sturdy bar/doorframe with feet on the floor (10–20 seconds) if shoulders tolerate it.

Tips for consistency
- Pair microbreaks with triggers: meeting ends, coffee refill, file saves.
- Use a timer or app with a 30–45 minute reminder.
- Stand for calls and walk during at least one meeting per day.
- Aim to accumulate 6,000–8,000+ steps daily if possible—movement complements stretching.

Safety and form cues
- Stretch should ease with steady breathing; back off if sharp pain, tingling, or numbness.
- Keep ribs down on chest/hip stretches to avoid over-arching your lower back.
- For knee sensitivity, use extra padding or do standing versions.
- If you have a recent injury or persistent symptoms, check with a clinician first.

Want this tailored? Tell me your tightest areas (neck/shoulders, hips, low back, wrists) and what space/equipment you have, and I’ll customize a 5- and a 12-minute version for you.
